title: He didn’t have to pay.
paragraphs: Because deep down… you and I do the opposite.

We fight for our rights.
We protect our image.
We defend our pride.
Even when God is asking for surrender.

He was the Son.
Free.
Untouchable.
Yet in Matthew 17:27, He tells Peter, “Go to the sea… the first fish you catch… you will find a coin. Take it and give it to them for Me and for yourself.”
The King paid a tax He didn’t owe… using a coin He already owned… from a fish He already commanded.
Why would the One who owns everything choose to act like He owed something?
And if you’re honest… it exposes something in us.
Because some of us obey only when it benefits us.
Some of us submit only when it’s convenient.
Some of us say “God is in control”… but panic the moment provision looks impossible.

And some of us—
we quietly hold onto pride disguised as “discernment.”
When was the last time you obeyed God even when you knew you were right?
When was the last time you chose humility over being justified?
This moment at the shore… it’s a whisper of something heavier.

Because the same Jesus who pulled provision from a fish…
would later stretch out His hands on wood.
Not to pay a temple tax.
Scripture says in 2 Corinthians 8:9 that though He was rich, yet for your sake He became poor, so that you by His poverty might become rich.

He became what you couldn’t bear…
so you could receive what you didn’t earn.
Jesus didn’t just demonstrate power over creation.
He demonstrated surrender under the Father.
Philippians 2:6–8 tells us that though He was in the form of God, He did not count equality with God a thing to be grasped… but emptied Himself… becoming obedient to the point of death.
So don’t tell me obedience is weakness.
Pride is the silent killer sitting in church.
You can lift your hands and still resist God.
You can quote Scripture and still avoid surrender.

You can look spiritual…
and still be far from submission.

Because the same Jesus who told Peter where to find provision…
is speaking to you right now about what you’ve been avoiding.
God’s provision is often waiting on the other side of your obedience.
Peter didn’t see the coin until he moved.
You won’t see breakthrough until you step.
If you only obey when you understand… you’re not walking by faith—you’re negotiating control.
Because this isn’t just about exposing pride.
It’s about inviting you into freedom.
And that’s what He’s doing with you.

Calling you out…
not to crush you—
but to free you.
Because your identity is not “the one who struggles to obey.”

You are called to be a son.
A daughter.
Led by the Spirit.
Romans 8:14 says those who are led by the Spirit of God are the children of God.

Not controlled by fear.
Not ruled by pride.
And here’s the Gospel, clear and unfiltered:
Your sin created a debt you could never pay.

No amount of good works.
No religious effort.
No “trying harder.”
He lived the life you couldn’t live.
And rose again so you could be forgiven, restored, and made new.
Ephesians 2:8–9 says you are saved by grace through faith—not by works, so no one can boast.
So stop trying to earn what Jesus already paid for.
And if you feel that pull in your chest right now—that weight, that conviction—that’s not guilt to crush you.
That’s the Holy Spirit calling you home.
For those who are done with surface-level faith and ready to grow roots.
Follow if you’re ready to grow.
There’s more coming… and the next message might be the one you didn’t know you needed.
